new_page.h1: Port Kells, Surrey: Industrial Area and Village Guide
new_page.title: Port Kells Surrey Industrial Property and Area Guide
new_page.description: Port Kells, Surrey: the industrial area north of Highway 1 and the village south of it. Zoning, flood, pipelines, access and what to check before you buy.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Written November 10, 2026 from City of Surrey, provincial and federal sources and the market reports listed on the page. Jared’s verdict is still to come.

Port Kells is the north-east corner of Surrey, on the south bank of the Fraser River at the Langley border, east of 176 Street. Highway 1 splits it in two. North of the highway, down to the river, is the Port Kells industrial area: warehouses, distribution, trucking and light industry along 96 Avenue and 192 Street. South of the highway is the original village, with a school, a park and homes on large rural lots.

The name goes back to two settlers, both called Henry Kells, who laid out a townsite on the river around 1889 and 1890 and expected a port to follow. It never did. The 1907 schoolhouse and St. Oswald’s Anglican Church (1911) are what is left of the old village.
Industrial and commercial property in Port Kells

Invest Surrey, the City’s business arm, describes Port Kells as one of Surrey’s major industrial areas: about 781 acres and roughly 610 businesses, mostly on light industrial (IL) zoning, with manufacturing, construction and wholesale and distribution the main uses. The City calls 192 Street the main north-south road serving the industrial area.

There is no published price or rent for Port Kells on its own, so these are the Surrey-wide numbers. In the second quarter of 2026 Surrey had 53 commercial sales, more than any other Fraser Valley city, 19 of them industrial, for $249.9 million in all. In the third quarter, 4.2% of Surrey’s industrial space was vacant, against 5.7% in Langley, and asking rents averaged $19.66 a square foot net plus $6.95 in additional rent.

blocks.text: Two things to take from that. Surrey has 46% of all the industrial space being built across Metro Vancouver, and in the third quarter more Surrey space was given back than leased (net absorption of −220,336 sq ft). That gives a business looking to buy or lease more choice, and gives a landlord more competition for tenants.

blocks.text: Before you buy industrial property in Port Kells

items.t: Zoning and permitted uses. Most of the area is IL, but some sites carry their own comprehensive development (CD) zoning. Check that your exact use is permitted on the exact property with the City of Surrey before you firm up.

Development cost charges. Surrey sets Port Kells-specific charges for industrial and commercial development, separate from its city-wide rates. If you plan to build or expand, put them in the numbers early.

Flood. The Fraser River frontage east of 132 Street has no dyke, and the City requires development there to be built to flood protection levels. Ask the City for the flood construction level and check title for a floodplain covenant.

Pipelines. Trans Mountain’s pipeline and a pump station sit in the district. Digging or building within 30 metres of a federally regulated pipeline, or driving equipment across one, needs the pipeline company’s written consent first.

Site history. If a site has had certain industrial uses, BC’s contaminated sites rules can require a Site Disclosure Statement before a rezoning, subdivision or permit that disturbs soil. Ask what the site has been used for, and get an environmental professional’s advice before you firm up.
Rail. CN owns most of the river frontage, and its main line runs along it. Expect trains as background, and confirm any rail access with CN, not the listing.
GST. GST usually applies when you buy commercial or industrial property, on top of property transfer tax. Get your accountant’s advice on it before you write the offer.

blocks.text: South of the highway, the old village sits around 88 Avenue, with homes on large lots and farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve along its southern edge. The City’s South Port Kells plan (2005) covers about 608 hectares from the highway down to the ALR. In April 2026 Council authorized planning studies ahead of a neighbourhood plan for the rest of South Port Kells, after the Port Kells Community Association asked for one and owners of 94 of the 192 lots answered the City’s survey. No plan has been drawn yet, so buy a property for what it is today.

Very little sells here. In the twelve months to October 22, 2026 the MLS® sub-area recorded 6 home and land sales: 3 acreages, 2 lots and 1 house. That is too few for a fair median, so ask me for the sold list.

blocks.text: Port Kells Elementary, kindergarten to grade 7, is in the village at 19076 88 Avenue, in the schoolhouse that opened in 1907. There is no secondary school in Port Kells. Surrey Schools sets catchments by address, so check the exact property in the district’s school locator.

items.t: Port Kells Park, 19340 88 Avenue, just west of the village centre: an outdoor pool, softball diamonds, a playground, outdoor fitness equipment and the Latimer Creek wetland.
Tynehead Regional Park, about 260 hectares of forest and meadow at the head of the Serpentine River, with the Tynehead Hatchery, a few minutes west along 96 Avenue.
The 192 Street ramps on Highway 1 face west only: on toward Vancouver, off from Vancouver. Heading east to Langley and the valley, you use the 200 Street interchange.
North across the Fraser, 96 Avenue runs into Golden Ears Way and the Golden Ears Bridge, toll-free since September 2017. Maple Ridge is about 13 minutes off-peak.
TransLink’s 501 bus runs along 96 Avenue between Surrey Central Station and Langley Centre. Nothing runs on the village streets.
The nearest SkyTrain will be Clayton Station, at 190 Street and Fraser Highway, when the Surrey Langley line opens (expected late 2029). It is a drive, not a walk.

faq.q: What is the zoning in Port Kells?
faq.a: North of Highway 1 it is mostly light industrial (IL), with some sites on their own comprehensive development (CD) zoning. South of the highway it is rural and residential land under the South Port Kells plan, with ALR land along the southern edge. Check the exact property with the City.

faq.q: Can I live on an industrial property in Port Kells?
faq.a: Don’t plan on it. The industrial zones are for business, and the homes are south of the highway. Check the permitted uses for the exact property with the City before you buy.

faq.q: How do trucks get onto Highway 1 east from Port Kells?
faq.a: Through the 200 Street interchange. The 192 Street ramps only face west, toward Vancouver.

faq.q: Is there a school in Port Kells?
faq.a: Yes. Port Kells Elementary, kindergarten to grade 7, at 19076 88 Avenue. There is no secondary school in Port Kells, so check the catchment for the exact address.
